newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares end sharply down on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares end sharply down on rumours.

text.p: Shanghai A and B shares closed sharply down on Wednesday on rumours that Beijing is planning measures to cool down the booming stock markets, brokers said.
The B index lost 5.804 points or 6.22 percent to 87.511 points on volume of 28.8 million shares worth $20.24 million.
The A index shed 88.789 points or 5.8 percent to 1,442.517 points on volume of 724.1 million shares worth 10.3 billion yuan.
Brokers said there were widespread rumours in the market that Beijing would take steps to crack down on the stock markets, which have risen more than 50 percent this year.
"The rumours dominated the market today, triggering heavy institutional selling and sending the index sharply down," said one broker. "Retail investors also followed up with selling."

"Everyone was saying that some institutions would face tough punishment due to their illegal trading," said a second broker. "If this rumour is confirmed, the market will continue to fall in the next few days."

Of the 43 shares on the B share market, 42 traded with 41 down and one up. Shanghai Lianhua Fibre Co. was the biggest loser on speculative selling, plunging $0.018 to hit a limit-down level of $0.160 on volume of 70,000 shares.
Shanghai Worldbest Co. was the most actively traded on heavy profit-taking selling despite some institutional support, falling $0.046 or 6.21 percent to $0.694 on volume of 4.8 million shares.
On the A share market, the SSE 30 blue-chip index slipped 230.643 points or 5.51 percent to 3,952.505 points.
Wuxi Taiji Industry was the worst performer on institutional selling, plunging 1.10 yuan or 10.01 percent to 9.88 yuan on volume of 8.0 million shares.
